hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: In a line of people, visibility from one side is governed by Stirling numbers of the first kind.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: When people are arranged by distinct heights, each cycle in permutation corresponds to a visible peak.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Calculate the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind |s(n, k)| modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def visiblePeopleWays(n: int, k: int) -> int:
    MOD = 1_000_000_007
    if k == 0 or k > n:
        return 0
    dp = [0] * (k + 1)
    dp[1] = 1
    for i in range(2, n + 1):
        next_dp = [0] * (k + 1)
        for j in range(1, min(k, i) + 1):
            next_dp[j] = (dp[j - 1] + (i - 1) * dp[j]) % MOD
        dp = next_dp
    return dp[k]
```

complexity.notes: Computes Stirling numbers in O(n * k) with space-optimized 1D row.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Enumerating n! permutations exceeds time limits for n > 10.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintains an array of length k + 1.
